---
title: "The docs as one PDF"
---


`print/make_pdf.py` renders a language project as a single linked PDF —
the file behind the PDF icon in this site's header:

```sh
python3 print/make_pdf.py docs/en site/en/docs.pdf
```

## What it does, and why this way

**The chapter order is the sidebar order.** The script reads the
project's `_quarto.yml`, takes the sidebar's pages in sequence and
assembles a temporary Quarto book from them; top-level sidebar
sections become book parts carrying the section's title. There is no
second list of chapters to maintain, so the PDF cannot fall behind a
page that was added — the same principle as the
[language map](multilingual.qmd).

**The cover cannot drift from the site.** Its title is
`website.title`, its subtitle comes from the front matter of the
language's `index.qmd` (falling back to "Documentation"). If the
project keeps its page graphics in an `asset/` directory, that
directory is copied into the book, so every figure of the site appears
in the PDF too.

**The engine is Typst**, which ships inside Quarto — no TeX toolchain
to install, on your machine or in CI. The table of contents and the
citations are clickable links, and if the site uses a bibliography,
per-page reference lists are stripped and one bibliography sits at the
end of the book.

**Noto Sans is embedded** from `print/fonts/`, so the PDF matches the
site and renders the same everywhere.

One Quarto quirk is codified in the script rather than in your memory:
the Typst book template requires an `author` and fails with a cryptic
error without one. The script takes it as an optional third argument
or from the `author:` in the language's `index.qmd` front matter, and
fails with a message naming both options when neither is set.

## Wiring it into a site

Give the navbar an icon pointing at the file; Quarto adjusts the
relative path on every page:

```yaml
navbar:
  right:
    - icon: file-pdf
      aria-label: PDF
      href: docs.pdf
```

and call the script from your build after the site render, once per
language:

```sh
python3 print/make_pdf.py docs/en site/en/docs.pdf
python3 print/make_pdf.py docs/de site/de/Dokumentation.pdf
```

The PDF is rebuilt with the site, so it is always the same release as
the pages around it — under a [versioned deployment](versions.qmd),
every version directory keeps the PDF that belongs to it.
